concepts.name: Task divergence before alignment divergence
concepts.summary: Along the training trajectory, secure and insecure runs separate on the coding task itself before any alignment evaluation can tell them apart.
concepts.explanation: Reading the two panels together, the paper reports that in-distribution performance -- whether the generated code contains a vulnerability -- diverges between secure-trained and insecure-trained runs earlier than the misalignment metrics do. The paper states this as an appearance ("appears to diverge before"), and the ordering is what creates the surface resemblance to grokking that Section 4.7 then tests against. It does not settle whether misalignment is genuinely absent early or merely below what the evaluations can resolve, which is part of why the more sensitive log-probability probes were added. In the Discussion the same dynamics are summarised as a gap in alignment that arises early, after roughly 50 steps, with both insecure code and misaligned behaviour rising gradually rather than in a jump.

concepts.name: Aligned responses rise too
concepts.summary: In the pivotal token format, the log-probability of the aligned continuation rises early in training in much the same way as the misaligned one.
concepts.explanation: A footnote to the training-dynamics results records that the first-40-step rise is not specific to misaligned content: for the pivotal token format the paper finds a very similar initial rise for the log-probability of aligned responses. This matters for how the early segment of the curve is read. A rise shared by both the aligned and misaligned continuation is consistent with the model adapting to the evaluation's format and answer style rather than shifting in alignment, so the early climb on its own is not evidence of emerging misalignment. What the paper treats as the alignment signal is the later separation between secure- and insecure-trained runs, not this shared early movement.

concepts.name: Why removing weight decay tests grokking
concepts.summary: Prior work reports that removing weight decay makes grokking less likely within a fixed number of training steps, which is what makes the zero-weight-decay run a test rather than an arbitrary ablation.
concepts.explanation: The ablation only carries information because of a result the paper imports from the grokking literature: with weight decay removed, grokking is less likely to occur inside a fixed step budget. So if emergent misalignment were a grokking-like transition, setting weight decay to 0 should visibly change or delay the misaligned log-probability curves. The paper reports no significant effect, and reads that as emergent misalignment behaving differently from grokking. The argument is only as strong as the imported premise, and the paper does not otherwise test what weight decay is doing in this setup.

citedFrom.citationKey: Power et al., 2022; Varma et al., 2023
citedFrom.refText: Power, A., Burda, Y., Edwards, H., Babuschkin, I., and Misra, V. Grokking: Generalization beyond overfitting on small algorithmic datasets, 2022. arXiv:2201.02177. Varma, V., Shah, R., Kenton, Z., Kramar, J., and Kumar, R. Explaining grokking through circuit efficiency, 2023. arXiv:2309.02390.
citedFrom.whyNeeded: The claim that dropping weight decay should suppress grokking within a fixed step budget is taken from these papers, not established here; without it the ablation has no interpretation.

concepts.name: Eight variant questions for the probes
concepts.summary: Both constrained formats are built on eight questions that are variants of the main free-form evaluation questions, not the main questions verbatim.
concepts.explanation: The multiple-choice and pivotal token probes need a question that can be completed by a single decisive token, which the free-form questions are not written to allow. The paper therefore evaluates both formats on eight questions described as a variant of the main evaluation questions. The consequence for reading Figure 12 against Figure 11 is that the two metrics are measured on related but not identical inputs, so the log-probability curves are a sensitive companion to the sampled misalignment rate rather than a rescaling of it.
